It is further alleged that the applicant's wife Kathun Bee is the Director of the aforesaid Co-operative Society and the complaint has been registered against Kathun Bee.
3 . Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant is a government teacher and has been falsely implicated in this case.

The allegation against the applicant is that he, on the promise of higher returns, instigated some persons to deposit money in the co-operative society, which is being operated by his wife Kathun Bee, whereby committed cheating and by misusing the money committed breach of promise, however, as per record, no transaction has been made in his account and the said transactions are being made in the account operated by his wife Kathun Bee who is suffering from cancer.
Applicant is in custody since 04.06.2023 and final conclusion of trial will take sufficient long time.
Therefore, it is prayed that the application be allowed and the applicant be released on bail.

4 . Counsel for the respondent/State, on the other hand, opposes the prayer by submitting that main Kathun Bee happens to be the wife of the present applicant and she is absconding, hence no case is made out for grant of bail to the applicant.
5.

In reply, learned counsel for the applicant submitted that anticipatory bail of Kathun Bee has been dismissed as withdrawn with liberty to surrender before the trial Court, but since she is suffering from cancer and as she is undergoing chemotherapy, she could not surrender herself before the trial Court.
However, counsel assured that if the present applicant is released on bail, the applicant will surrender the main accused before the trial Court.

5. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and looking to the facts and circumstances of the case, nature of the offence, the age of the applicant and his custody period, I am of the view that it is a case, in which applicant may be released on bail.
Consequently, without commenting on the merits of the case, first bail application under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of bail filed on behalf of applicant, stands allowed.

6. It is directed that applicant be released on bail on his/her furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his/her regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he/she shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial.

The applicant shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 437(3) of Cr.P.C.
7.
This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case of bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
Certified copy as per rules.
